content.content:
1. License: no element of the dependent contradicts a parent named in depends_on — here the atomicity clause of usvvozwn and, through it, the refusal and document-presence predicate of mmrklvqs. Fail on any contradicting element: an element that stands the naming on a refusal other than the invocation's, that has anything created for any id the invocation names (a change opened, a node document written, an edge landed, a marker or journal entry recorded) before or beside the naming, or that re-decides when the refusal happens. Name the element and the parent it contradicts.
2. Every unknown id, not a subset: fail if the requirement is satisfied while fewer than all of the invocation's unknown `--evaluates` ids are named — the first unknown id only, the last only, one per duplicated id, a sample, or any subset selected by a rule (first-seen, last-seen, resolved-before-unknown, distinct-after-deduplication, until a length threshold). The order in which the named ids appear is not fixed, and naming them in the invocation's own order, in sorted order or in any other order is equally a naming.
3. The ids themselves, not a proxy: fail if the refusal names a count of unknown ids, a set size, a number followed by a noun, a boolean or a status word (“some `--evaluates` id is unknown”, “an unknown id”, “1 unknown id”, “unknown ids”), a position or index, or a pointer the caller must resolve elsewhere, instead of naming the spellings of the unknown ids so that each can be read off the refusal and corrected without re-deriving which ids failed.
4. Only the unknown ones: fail if an id that names a node document is presented in the refusal as unknown, unresolved or missing — including a refusal that reports the whole `--evaluates` set as not naming a node, or that lists a resolved id among the ids it could not find. Quoting the invocation's full id set while distinguishing what resolved from what did not is not this failure.
5. Unknown means no node document, and no id is excused: fail if the requirement fixes which ids count as unknown by anything but whether a node document answers for the id — by the id's kind or content, by whether it is also named with `--on`, by whether it appears in some node's `depends_on`, or by a special case for the root sentinel `zzzzzzzz`, which names no node document and so is named with the other unknown ids when the invocation names it with `--evaluates`. Fail also if the requirement leaves the extension of “unknown” to be decided at naming time by a rule of its own rather than by the prerequisite's predicate.
6. In the refusal, not beside it: fail if the ids are named anywhere other than the refusing output the prerequisite fixes — a line following the refusal, a second message after it, a hint or usage block offered instead of it, a log line, an entry in `.deccy/journal/`, a marker in `.deccy/markers.json`, a separate diagnostic the caller runs afterwards, or output of a later invocation — so that the refusal itself refuses without naming anything and the naming is found elsewhere. Which stream the refusal writes to, and where within it the ids sit, are not fixed.
7. The `--evaluates` ids, not another flag's: fail if the refusal names the ids the invocation gave to `--on`, the ids of nodes the birth would depend on, the summary, or a merged list in which the `--evaluates` ids cannot be told apart, rather than the ids the invocation gave to `--evaluates` and that named no document. A refusal that names both sets while distinguishing them is not this failure.
8. Naming is the whole criterion: no element of the dependent is judged beyond the naming it adds. A refusal that names every unknown `--evaluates` id, and no id that resolves, satisfies these criteria whatever its message format, stream, ordering of named ids, exit status, count wording or evidence quoting — fail to apply a criterion here to any of those, and fail to demand of the dependent that it fix any of them.
content.rationale: Naming is the half of the refusal that makes an unknown `--evaluates` id repairable, and every way it can be lost is a way the caller cannot repair the invocation without guessing: a subset, a count, a resolved id reported as unknown, the ids of the wrong flag, or the ids printed somewhere other than the refusal. The prerequisite fixes the refusal the naming attaches to — one refusal, the invocation's, before anything is created — and, through the guard it depends on, the predicate that gives “each unknown id” a determinate extension at that moment; the criteria use both without re-deciding either, which is why the license line runs first and why nothing here reaches into atomicity, linkage, kind split, form or skeleton. Both endpoints are requirement sentences, so the cell is the matrix default — the gate form plus a flag to extend the matrix — and the check is a review of the recorded dependent against the recorded prerequisite, applied by a reader; nothing is executed for this form.
